# Assess and manage AI product risk

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before deploying or materially changing an AI-enabled product or internal decision workflow. An approved use-case risk assessment, evaluation record and monitored deployment decision with stop conditions.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Define the AI use case and affected people

agent-runnable


Record the intended users, decisions supported, model and data providers, prohibited uses and the consequences of errors. Identify whether personal data, regulated activity or high-consequence decisions need specialist review.

- Sources: [NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-ai-rmf-10) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Agree risk ownership and acceptance criteria

human · human approval required


Product, security, domain and legal reviewers decide the applicable controls and release criteria. Assign human authority for sensitive decisions and define when the system must abstain, escalate or stop.

- Sources: [NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-ai-rmf-10) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Build and run representative evaluations

agent-runnable


Prepare authorized test data and scenarios covering expected use, misuse, failure, privacy and security. Record model versions, prompts, metrics and known limits and avoid exposing production secrets in evaluation logs.

- Sources: [NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-ai-rmf-10) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Review results and authorize a limited deployment

human · human approval required


The accountable reviewers evaluate unresolved failures, safeguards and rollback readiness. Approve only the specified scope and access, with an owner for user communication and incident handling.

- Sources: [NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-ai-rmf-10) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Monitor outcomes and reassess material changes

agent-runnable


Track errors, user feedback, incidents and drift against the accepted thresholds. Re-run relevant evaluations when models, data, prompts or use cases change and pause uses that violate the agreed stop conditions.

- Verify: An approved use-case risk assessment, evaluation record and monitored deployment decision with stop conditions.
- Sources: [NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-ai-rmf-10) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)
